Computing the first derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(4\sqrt{x}+5{x}^{2}+x)}^{′} \\  & ={(4{x}^{1/2}+5{x}^{2}+x)}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4{x}^{-1/2}+2\cdot 5x+1 \\  & =2{x}^{-1/2}+10x+1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & ={(2{x}^{-1/2}+10x+1)}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2{x}^{-3/2}+10+0 \\  & =-{x}^{-3/2}+10 \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}+10.\end{aligned}
$$
